description: Create or update the root `README.md` for a repository — a brief description, badges (CI status, SonarCloud/SonarQube, npm, Maven Central, Packagist, PyPI, WordPress.org, PHP/Python version, GHCR container image, Swift Package Index, crates.io/docs.rs, pkg.go.dev, NuGet, GitHub release, etc.), a project status table (language, versions, framework, platforms, license, CI, quality tools, distribution; for a command-line tool also the toolchain floor, argument parser, terminal-UI library, release targets and channels), documentation links (Antora site, the generated CLI reference page, Maven site report, SonarCloud dashboard, generated API docs such as TypeDoc/Compodoc/Storybook/Dokka/DocC/DocFX/rustdoc/pkg.go.dev/phpDocumentor/Sphinx, OpenAPI/Swagger UI, CHANGELOG), installation instructions (Maven/Gradle/npm/Composer/uv/pip/SwiftPM/etc. dependency snippets, a "run it locally"/container-image/store-listing section for services, web apps, WordPress plugins/themes and PrestaShop modules, or — for a command-line tool — only the release channels actually wired: Homebrew tap, `cargo install`, `go install`, Scoop/WinGet, `dotnet tool install -g`, or the release archive with `SHA256SUMS`/`gh attestation verify`, plus build from source — matched to the project's actual stack and build tool — Spring Boot (Java or Kotlin, Maven or Gradle KTS), Quarkus, Laravel, WordPress, PrestaShop, NestJS, Next.js, FastAPI, Django, plain Python packages, command-line tools in Rust/Go/Swift/.NET, plain Rust crates and Go modules, and the earlier library/app stacks), and a short "how it works" section with a runnable example (for a command-line tool: a human example, a `--json` example piped to `jq`, the exit-code table, and a note on using it from scripts and AI agents). Invoke as `/iru-setup-readme`, optionally with `args` (one key/value pair per line, all optional) — `sonar` set to `none` suppresses Sonar badges and dashboard links even when a `sonar {}` block or `sonar-project.properties` exists, `ci` set to `no` omits CI status badges, `pages` set to `no` avoids linking a github.io documentation site (or Next.js static export) that won't be published, and `on-existing` (`ask`/`keep`/`update`/`replace`, scripted runs, default `ask`) pre-answers the existing-README question — so an orchestrator's resolved choices produce a README matching them. Explores the repository's actual state (`pom.xml`/`build.gradle*`/`gradle.properties`/`composer.json`/`package.json`/`pyproject.toml`/`uv.lock`/ `Package.swift`/`Cargo.toml`/`go.mod`/`Directory.Build.props`/WordPress plugin or theme headers/PrestaShop module class/Android Gradle modules/Xcode or Tuist project files/etc., git remote, GitHub Actions workflows, Sonar config, Antora docs, `CHANGELOG.md`, `LICENSE`, source code) to fill in every section — a section whose source material doesn't exist yet (e.g. a brand-new, mostly empty repository) is omitted rather than filled with placeholders or invented content; a WordPress `readme.txt` is a separate file this skill never replaces. Announces whether it is creating the README from scratch or updating an existing one; if `README.md` already exists (including a generator's stock README from `laravel new`, `create-next-app`, `nest new`, `quarkus create` or `uv init`), warns the user and shows the proposed content as a diff before writing anything, asking whether to Update it (merged draft, hand-written sections kept), Keep it as is, or Replace it (regenerated, hand-written sections dropped). Use whenever a repository needs a README bootstrapped or refreshed from what's actually there, instead of hand-writing it.
